about: Every built Vela component, generated from guidelines/components/*.md by scripts/build-components-json.mjs. Do not edit: change the spec and run npm run components. Each spec is the full contract; this is its index.

components.name: Brand Mark
components.purpose: Another company's own logo, drawn as its owner drew it, used only to link to that company's service: "Vela on GitHub", "Vela in Figma". It is a separate closed set, kept apart from Icon. It never moves, sits in the interface's own icon grey, and never stands for Vela itself.

status.label: Experimental
status.note: specced, built and tested in the core entry; no Figma set yet (the builder, scripts/figma/components/brand-mark.figma.js, is ready and has not been run). Its consumer is [Icon Button](icon-button.md)'s brandMark glyph, and the playground's header links to GitHub and Figma through it.

components.whenToUse:
- **A link to that company's own service, from a product built with Vela** → **Brand Mark**, inside an **Icon Button** link.
- **Sign in with a provider** → not this. Out of scope.
- **A list of integrations or connectors** → not this.
- **npm, or any service whose logo needs permission** → the word, set by Icon Button, not a mark.
- **Vela's own logo or wordmark** → never a Brand Mark.

A glyph-only link to GitHub or Figma is an [Icon Button](icon-button.md) with `brandMark`. Don't wrap a bare Brand Mark in an `<a>` of your own.

props.name: name
props.notes: **Required. These two only.**

props.name: size
props.notes: **These two only.** 16px or 20px, Icon's size tokens. `figma` is `large` only.

props.name: label
props.notes: **Standalone only.** The accessible name. Exclusive with `decorative`.

props.name: decorative
props.notes: **Inside a named control only.** `aria-hidden`. Exclusive with `label`.

components.name: Button
components.purpose: Triggers an action: save, submit, delete, apply, cancel. Carries a text label and an optional **left** icon. `variant` encodes the action's consequence; `appearance` encodes visual weight.
components.whenToUse:
- Action that stays in the page flow → **Button**.
- Navigates to another page → a router `<Link>`, not a Button.
- Flips a binary setting that takes effect immediately → **Toggle**.
- Icon-only, no label → an [**Icon Button**](icon-button.md) (`@omkarux/vela/headless`).

props.name: variant
props.notes: Consequence. **These three only.**

props.name: appearance
props.notes: Weight. **These three only.** `text-link` is primary-only.

props.name: size
props.notes: **These four only.**

props.name: disabled
props.notes: A state, not a variant. Leaves the tab order.

props.name: loading
props.notes: Shows an indicator, sets `aria-busy`, ignores clicks.

props.name: icon
props.notes: Always **left** of the label. There is no trailing slot.

props.name: type
props.notes: `"submit"` only for a form's commit button.

props.name: children
props.notes: Label. Verb-first, Title Case.

components.name: Checkbox
components.purpose: A box that **records intent** — on its own ("accept the terms") or as one of several in a **Checkbox Group** ("scan these three scopes") — and does nothing until a Save, Apply or Submit commits the form.

status.label: Experimental
status.note: the first component born in @omkarux/vela/headless (Base UI 1.9); there is no core implementation, and its Figma set is published in the library (built from scripts/figma/components/checkbox.figma.js). Approved once the API has settled; see GOVERNANCE.md.

components.whenToUse:
- Records a choice that a **Save / Apply / Submit** button commits later — accept terms, pick the
  scopes of a scan, select rows for a bulk action → **Checkbox**.
- Takes effect **the moment it is flipped** — notifications on/off, dark mode, "enable this rule"
  → **Toggle** (`toggle.md`). The test is the Save button: if one is needed, it is a Checkbox; if
  the change is live already, it is a Toggle. A Toggle behind a Save button is the single most
  common mistake agents make with these two.
- Several options where **exactly one** can be chosen → **Radio Group** (`radio-group.md`).
- Several options where **any number** can be chosen → **Checkbox.Group**.
- One box that stands for a set — "select all", with some rows selected → `indeterminate`, which
  renders `aria-checked="mixed"` and a dash.
- A long list to pick from (more than ~7 options, or searchable) → a Multi-select, which is **not
  in this kit**. Flag the gap; do not build it out of Checkboxes.

props.name: label
props.notes: **Required.** The visible label, also the accessible name.

props.name: checked
props.notes: Controlled. Exclusive with `defaultChecked`. Ignored inside a Group, which owns the state.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.notes: Uncontrolled initial state. Exclusive with `checked`.

props.name: onCheckedChange
props.notes: Receives the **next** value.

props.name: indeterminate
props.notes: The "some of the set" state: `aria-checked="mixed"` and a dash. Visual only — the next click reports `true` or `false`.

props.name: disabled
props.notes: Native `disabled`: leaves the tab order, swallows clicks.

props.name: size
props.notes: **These two only.** The same two as Toggle.

props.name: description
props.notes: A hint under the label, linked by `aria-describedby`.

props.name: error
props.notes: **The message.** Presence puts the box in the error state; the string is announced.

props.name: name
props.notes: Native, forwarded to the hidden `<input>` for form submission.

props.name: value
props.notes: Native, forwarded. **Required inside a Group** — it is how the group knows the box.

props.name: label
props.notes: **Required.** Rendered as the group's visible label and wired as its accessible name.

props.name: value
props.notes: Controlled: the `value`s of the checked boxes. Exclusive with `defaultValue`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.notes: Uncontrolled initial state. Exclusive with `value`.

props.name: onValueChange
props.notes: Receives the **next** array.

props.name: disabled
props.notes: Disables every box in the group.

props.name: orientation
props.notes: **These two only.** Layout; keyboard order is document order either way.

props.name: children
props.notes: `Checkbox` elements, each with a `value`.

components.name: Contextual Alert
components.purpose: An inline banner carrying a severity. Lives in the page flow, next to the thing it is about — it is not a toast and not a modal.
components.whenToUse:
- An event or condition the user must read, inline → **Contextual Alert**.
- An object's ongoing health, usually in a table → **Status Indicator**.
- Transient confirmation that something already happened, floating and leaving on its own →
  **Toast** (`toast.md`, `@omkarux/vela/headless`): `success`, `info` or `warning` only. Anything
  `minor`, `major` or `critical`, and any failure, stays here, in the page.
- A blocking decision → a Modal, **not in this kit**. Flag the gap.

props.name: severity
props.notes: **Required. These six only.**

props.name: title
props.notes: Optional bold lead-in.

props.name: children
props.notes: **Required.** The body.

props.name: onDismiss
props.notes: Omit for alerts the user must not clear.

props.name: dismissLabel
props.notes: Accessible name for the close control.

components.name: Dialog
components.purpose: A **modal** window for a decision that blocks the task — edit one thing and save, or cancel — with the page behind it dimmed, inert and scroll-locked until it closes. Its `alert` variant confirms a destructive or irreversible action, with an explicit way out.

status.label: Experimental
status.note: born in @omkarux/vela/headless (Base UI 1.9) with Popover and Tooltip; there is no core implementation, and its Figma set is published in the library (built from scripts/figma/components/dialog.figma.js). Approved once the API has settled; see GOVERNANCE.md.

components.whenToUse:
- The user must **answer before going on** — save or discard an edit, name a new policy, choose
  between two outcomes → **Dialog**.
- The answer **destroys or cannot be undone** — delete a policy, revoke every session, wipe a
  device → **Dialog `variant="alert"`**: a question, a safe cancel, and a destructive confirm.
- A panel the user may consult **while the page stays usable** — filters, details, a quick edit
  that does not block → **Popover** (`popover.md`).
- A long form, a multi-step flow, or anything the user would want a URL for → a **page** (or a
  side panel, which is **not in this kit**), not a Dialog. A dialog that scrolls for screens is a
  page in the wrong container.
- A message the user should read but need not answer → a **Contextual Alert** on the page
  (`contextual-alert.md`). A dialog that only says "OK" interrupts for nothing.
- A notification that comes and goes on its own, confirming something already done → **Toast**
  (`toast.md`). A toast never asks; a question is a Dialog.

props.name: variant
props.notes: **These two only.** `alert` is for a destructive or irreversible confirmation.

props.name: title
props.notes: **Required.** Rendered as the dialog's heading and wired as its accessible name.

props.name: description
props.notes: A sentence under the title, wired by `aria-describedby`.

props.name: size
props.notes: **These two only.** The width: `--vela-dialog-width` (480) or `--vela-dialog-width-wide` (720).

props.name: trigger
props.notes: The element that opens it — a `Button`. Omit it when `open` is driven from elsewhere.

props.name: open
props.notes: Controlled. Exclusive with `defaultOpen`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.notes: Uncontrolled initial state. Exclusive with `open`.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.notes: Receives the **next** state.

props.name: children
props.notes: The body. It scrolls; the header and the footer stay.

props.name: footer
props.notes: **`standard` only.** The actions, right-aligned. Wrap one in `Dialog.Close` to close on click.

props.name: closeLabel
props.notes: **`standard` only.** The accessible name of the header's close button.

props.name: cancelLabel
props.notes: **Required with `alert`.** The safe action: focused on open, and what Escape does.

props.name: confirmLabel
props.notes: **Required with `alert`.** The destructive action, verb-first ("Delete Policy").

props.name: onConfirm
props.notes: **Required with `alert`.** Called on confirm; the dialog then closes.

props.name: children
props.notes: **Required.** The one element that closes the dialog when activated. Inside a `Dialog` only.

components.name: Dropdown List
components.purpose: A short list that opens from a button. One option is current, and choosing another acts at once: it opens that tab or that view, and the list closes. Its first use is the Tabs overflow control ("6 more"), which lists every tab in the row.

status.label: Experimental
status.note: built, and its Figma set is published (31 Oct 2026). It is born in @omkarux/vela/headless (Base UI 1.9 Menu) with no core implementation. It is Approved once the API has settled and the manual screen-reader check in Accessibility is done; see GOVERNANCE.md.

components.whenToUse:
- Choose **one of a set where one is current**, and the choice **acts at once**: go to a hidden
  tab, switch to another saved view. → **Dropdown List**.
- A **form value** chosen now and submitted later, with a label, validation and an empty state →
  a Select List, **not in this kit**. Flag the gap. A Dropdown List has no "nothing chosen" and is
  never inside a form.
- A list of **commands** (Edit / Duplicate / Delete) → an Actions Dropdown, **not in this kit**.
  Nothing in a Dropdown List is "current", so it would be the wrong role.
- **Several** choices at once, or filters → a **Popover** with a **Checkbox.Group**.
- Two to five options that fit on screen → **Tabs** (sections) or **Radio Group** (a setting).
  Don't hide what fits.
- More than about 50 options, or options that need searching → a combobox, **not in this kit**.
  Flag it.
- A list of **different sections of the same page**, all visible → **Tabs**. A Dropdown List is
  what Tabs uses for the tabs that don't fit, not a replacement for Tabs.
- A list of **pages to go to** (site or app navigation) → links, with `aria-current="page"` on the
  one you are on. That is navigation, **not this component**: a Dropdown List's items are radio
  items, not links.

The items are one radio group inside the menu. The group needs no name of its own: the menu's
`label` names the only choice there is.

props.name: label
props.notes: **Required.** Names the list for assistive technology ("All tabs"). Not shown.

props.name: trigger
props.notes: **Required.** One element that renders a `<button>`. It gets `aria-haspopup="menu"`, `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls`.

props.name: items
props.notes: **Required, at least one.** In display order.

props.name: value
props.notes: The current option (controlled). Must be one of the items' `value`s. Pass `value` or `defaultValue`: there is always a current option.

props.name: defaultValue
props.notes: The current option (uncontrolled). **Exclusive with `value`.**

props.name: onValueChange
props.notes: Called when an option is chosen. Not called for the current one.

props.name: open
props.notes: Controlled, as Popover. **Exclusive with `defaultOpen`.**

props.name: defaultOpen
props.notes: Uncontrolled initial state. **Exclusive with `open`.**

props.name: align
props.notes: **These two only.** Which edge of the trigger the list lines up with. Tabs uses `end`.

components.name: Icon
components.purpose: One glyph from a closed, curated set of fifty, drawn from Lucide and compiled into the package, at one of three token-bound sizes. It sits beside text, in a table cell or in another component's icon slot; it is never a control and never a severity, risk or status mark.

status.label: Experimental
status.note: specced, built and tested, and the glyph list is new; the Figma set is published in the library (built from scripts/figma/components/icon.figma.js). Approved once the kit's own inline glyphs (src/lib/icons.tsx) have moved onto it; see GOVERNANCE.md.

components.whenToUse:
- A glyph that reinforces adjacent text — "Blocked" beside `shield-x`, "Export" beside
  `download` → **Icon**, `aria-hidden` (no `label`).
- A glyph that stands alone in a cell or a header and carries meaning nothing beside it states →
  **Icon** with a `label`.
- The mark of an event the user must read → **Contextual Alert**, which owns the severity marks.
  An Icon in a severity colour is not a substitute (there is no severity `tone`).
- A risk score or an object's health → **Risk Pill** or **Status Indicator**. A shield is not a
  risk level and a circle is not a status dot.
- A clickable glyph (close, copy, more) → an [**Icon Button**](icon-button.md)
  (`@omkarux/vela/headless`), which takes the glyph as `icon`. Do not put a click handler on an
  Icon (it will not compile) or wrap it in a `<div>`.
- Inside a Button → pass the Icon to Button's `icon` slot with `tone="inherit"`, so the glyph takes
  the label colour; Button keeps owning the slot's size.

props.name: name
props.notes: **Required.** One of the fifty names in *Glyphs* below, exported as `ICON_NAMES`. Lucide's canonical names: `funnel` not `filter`, `trash` not `trash-2`, `rotate-ccw-clock` not `history`.

props.name: size
props.notes: **These three only.** 16, 12, 20px.

props.name: tone
props.notes: **These three only.** No severity, risk or status tone.

props.name: label
props.notes: The accessible name. Present → `role="img"` and `aria-label`; absent → `aria-hidden`.

props.name: className
props.notes: Layout only (a margin, an alignment). Never a size or a colour.

components.name: Icon Button
components.purpose: A button or a link drawn as a single glyph, for an action or a destination people recognise without a word: close, copy, more, search, settings, open on GitHub. It always has a name, given as `label`. Its tooltip shows that same name to sighted pointer and keyboard users, and is never heard twice.

status.label: Experimental
status.note: specced, built and tested in @omkarux/vela/headless; no Figma set yet (the builder, scripts/figma/components/icon-button.figma.js, is ready and has not been run). The playground's header links to GitHub, npm and Figma are its first use.

components.whenToUse:
- A widely known glyph in a tight place (close, copy, more, search, settings, a service's mark) → **Icon Button**.
- Less familiar, or touch-first → **Button** with a label.
- Destructive (delete, revoke) → **Button** `variant="destructive"` with words.
- A setting that stays on or off (pin, mute) → a toggle icon button, **not in this kit**; flag the gap.
- A glyph that only decorates text → **Icon**.
- Several in a row → **Icon Button** side by side, each its own tab stop.
- A link to GitHub or Figma → **Icon Button** with `brandMark`; to npm → **Icon Button** with `word="npm"`. Never a bare **Brand Mark** in an `<a>` of your own.

props.name: label
props.notes: **Required.** The accessible name and the tooltip's words.

props.name: icon
props.notes: Exactly one of `icon`, `brandMark` or `word`. One of Icon's fifty.

props.name: brandMark
props.notes: `"github"` or `"figma"`. Figma at `tiny` doesn't compile.

props.name: word
props.notes: This one only. In `--vela-font-family-mono`.

props.name: size
props.notes: 24px box with a 16px glyph, or 35px with a 20px glyph.

props.name: onClick
props.notes: Button form. Exclusive with `href`.

props.name: type
props.notes: Button form only.

props.name: disabled
props.notes: Button form only. Native. Rare.

props.name: href
props.notes: Link form: `<a href>`. Exclusive with `onClick`, `type`, `disabled`.

props.name: opensInNewTab
props.notes: Link form only. `target="_blank"`, `rel="noopener noreferrer"`, and ", opens in a new tab" added to the name; the tooltip shows it too.

props.name: tooltipPlacement
props.notes: Tooltip's own set.

components.name: Input
components.purpose: Single-line text entry with a label, optional hint, and an error state.
components.whenToUse:
- Single-line text or numeric-as-text → **Input**.
- Multi-line → **Text Area** (`components/text-area.md`).
- Numeric with a spinner → Number Stepper, **not in this kit**. Flag the gap.
- Choosing from a set → Radio or Dropdown, **not in this kit**.

props.name: label
props.notes: **Required.**

props.name: hint
props.notes: Helper text. Wired via `aria-describedby`.

props.name: error
props.notes: Presence sets the error state; the string is the message.

props.name: size
props.notes: **These three only.**

props.name: required
props.notes: Renders a `*` and sets the native attribute.

components.name: Popover
components.purpose: A small **non-modal** panel anchored to the button that opened it — filters for a table, the detail behind a count, a short form that edits one thing — dismissed by Escape, by a press outside, or by the trigger again, with the rest of the page still usable.

status.label: Experimental
status.note: born in @omkarux/vela/headless (Base UI 1.9) with Tooltip and Dialog; there is no core implementation, and its Figma set is published in the library (built from scripts/figma/components/popover.figma.js). Approved once the API has settled; see GOVERNANCE.md.

components.whenToUse:
- A panel the user **opens on purpose** and may **act in** — a filter set, a column picker, a
  short edit — while the page behind stays usable → **Popover**.
- A short **label or hint** on hover or focus, text only, nothing to act on → **Tooltip**
  (`tooltip.md`). If the trigger's purpose is to open the panel, it is a Popover; if the trigger
  does something else and the text only explains it, it is a Tooltip.
- A **decision that blocks the task** — confirm, fill in, or cancel before anything else happens
  → **Dialog** (`dialog.md`). A popover never traps focus and never locks the page.
- A list of **commands** that open from a button (Edit / Duplicate / Delete) → an Actions
  Dropdown, which is **not in this kit**. Flag the gap; do not build a menu out of a Popover.
- A picker of **one value from many** → a Select List, **not in this kit**. Flag it.
- Anything the user must see to do the task — an error, the only copy of a key — is never only
  in a Popover: the page has to carry it.

props.name: trigger
props.notes: **Required.** The one element that opens it — a `Button` or a native `<button>`. It keeps its own props; the popover adds `aria-expanded`, `aria-haspopup` and the toggle.

props.name: title
props.notes: **Required.** Rendered as the popover's heading and wired as its accessible name.

props.name: placement
props.notes: **These four only.** The side of the trigger. `start` / `end` follow the writing direction. It flips to the opposite side when there is no room.

props.name: align
props.notes: **These three only.** Where it lines up along that side.

props.name: size
props.notes: **These two only.** The width: `--vela-popover-width` (280) or `--vela-popover-width-wide` (400).

props.name: open
props.notes: Controlled. Exclusive with `defaultOpen`.

props.name: defaultOpen
props.notes: Uncontrolled initial state. Exclusive with `open`.

props.name: onOpenChange
props.notes: Receives the **next** state.

props.name: children
props.notes: The body, under the title. It scrolls when the room runs out; the title stays.

components.name: Radio Group
components.purpose: A short list of options where **exactly one** is chosen — an enforcement mode, a retention period, a severity to assign — all visible at once, committed by a Save.

status.label: Experimental
status.note: born in @omkarux/vela/headless (Base UI 1.9) alongside Checkbox; there is no core implementation, and its Figma set is published in the library (built from scripts/figma/components/radio-group.figma.js). Approved once the API has settled; see GOVERNANCE.md.

components.whenToUse:
- **Two to five options, one answer**, and the user should see them all before choosing →
  **Radio Group**. Seeing every option is the point: the choice is a comparison.
- **More than five options**, or options the user already knows by name (a country, a tenant,
  a time zone) → a **Select List**, which is **not in this kit**. Flag the gap; do not stack
  twelve radios.
- Any number of answers → **Checkbox.Group** (`checkbox.md`).
- Exactly two options that are really on/off and take effect immediately → **Toggle**
  (`toggle.md`). Two options that are two named things ("Monitor" / "Block") → Radio Group.
- A choice that switches *what is shown* rather than what is saved → Tabs or a View Switcher,
  not a Radio Group.

props.name: label
props.notes: **Required.** Rendered as the group's visible label and wired as its accessible name.

props.name: value
props.notes: Controlled: the selected radio's `value`. Exclusive with `defaultValue`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.notes: Uncontrolled initial selection. Exclusive with `value`. Omit both for no selection.

props.name: onValueChange
props.notes: Receives the **next** value.

props.name: disabled
props.notes: Disables every radio in the group.

props.name: orientation
props.notes: **These two only.** Layout; arrow keys move in both axes either way, as native radios do.

props.name: error
props.notes: **The message.** Presence puts the group in the error state; the string is announced.

props.name: name
props.notes: Native, forwarded to the hidden `<input type="radio">`s for form submission.

props.name: children
props.notes: `RadioGroup.Radio` elements.

props.name: value
props.notes: **Required.** What the group reports when this radio is chosen.

props.name: label
props.notes: **Required.** The visible label, also the accessible name.

props.name: disabled
props.notes: Native `disabled`: skipped by the arrow keys, out of the tab order.

props.name: description
props.notes: A hint under the label, linked by `aria-describedby`.

components.name: Risk Pill
components.purpose: A small read-only pill carrying one of exactly three risk levels, usually in a table cell or next to the thing that was scored — a user, an asset, a finding.
components.whenToUse:
- A risk **score** on an object → **Risk Pill**.
- An event the user must read → **Contextual Alert** (that is severity, six levels).
- An object's ongoing health → **Status Indicator** (that is status, five states).
- A removable filter chip or tag → a Token Pill, **not in this kit**. Flag the gap.

props.name: risk
props.notes: **Required. These three only.**

props.name: label
props.notes: Visible text. Omitted, the pill renders the level word (`"Low"` / `"Medium"` / `"High"`). A custom label must still name the level.

props.name: size
props.notes: **These two only.**

components.name: Status Indicator
components.purpose: A coloured dot representing one of exactly five health states, usually in a table cell or next to an object name.
components.whenToUse:
- An object's ongoing health → **Status Indicator**.
- An event the user must read → **Contextual Alert**.
- A risk score → **Risk Pill** (the Risk taxonomy, three levels).

props.name: status
props.notes: **Required. These five only.**

props.name: label
props.notes: Visible text. **Strongly preferred.**

props.name: size
props.notes: **These two only.**

components.name: Table
components.purpose: Rows of records under named columns — assets, findings, policies, approvals — on native table elements, with a caption that names it, an optional sort affordance per column, two densities, and a scroll region that keeps a wide table inside its host.

status.label: Experimental
status.note: specced, built and tested in the core entry, but the API may still change while Phase 2 (Approval Queue, Autonomy Ladder policy grid) and Phase 2b (Filter Bar, Review Queue) build on it. Its three Figma sets are published in the library (built from scripts/figma/components/table.figma.js). See GOVERNANCE.md.

components.whenToUse:
- Records the user compares **across columns** — sort by last seen, scan a status column, read
  a count → **Table**.
- One record's fields, label and value → a description list (`<dl>`), not a two-column table.
- Cells the user **edits or moves between with the arrow keys** like a spreadsheet → a Data Grid
  (`role="grid"`), which is **not in this kit**. Flag the gap; a Table is read, not navigated
  cell by cell.
- Thousands of rows, server paging, column resizing, virtualisation → still a Table for the
  markup, but the data layer is the host's: this component fetches nothing, pages nothing and
  virtualises nothing. Flag a virtualised grid as a gap rather than building one on top.
- A narrow host that wants **cards instead of rows** → a card list, **not in this kit**. Do not
  restyle a table into cards with CSS; see *Responsive behaviour*.
- A layout grid of unrelated things → CSS grid, never a table.

props.name: caption
props.notes: **Required.** Rendered as the `<caption>` and the label of the scroll region.

props.name: captionHidden
props.notes: Visually hides the caption; it still names the table and the region.

props.name: density
props.notes: **These two only.** Compact tightens vertical padding; type and targets hold.

props.name: layout
props.notes: **These two only.** `fixed` takes column widths from the first row.

props.name: stickyHeader
props.notes: Pins the header row to the top of the scroll region. The host bounds the height.

props.name: children
props.notes: `Table.Head` and `Table.Body`.

props.name: children
props.notes: `<thead>` / `<tbody>`. Rows only.

props.name: children
props.notes: `<thead>` / `<tbody>`. Rows only.

props.name: selected
props.notes: Part of the host's selection: `aria-selected="true"`, the row tint and a start-edge marker.

props.name: aria-current
props.notes: The row the page is about (open in a side panel). Passed through; draws the marker.

props.name: scope
props.notes: **These two only.** `row` for the cell that names a body row.

props.name: sort
props.notes: Column headers only. Renders a button in the `<th>`; `aria-sort` while sorted.

props.name: align
props.notes: **These two only.** `end` over a numeric column.

props.name: children
props.notes: **Required.** The label. **A `string` when `sort` is set** — the button's name is built from it.

props.name: numeric
props.notes: Tabular numerals, end-aligned, unwrapped. Takes no `align`.

props.name: align
props.notes: **These two only.**

props.name: colSpan
props.notes: **Required.** The header's column count.

props.name: children
props.notes: **Required.** What the empty table means — "No assets match these filters".

components.name: Tabs
components.whenToUse:
- Different content sections (Alerts / Assets / Audit) → **Tabs**.
- The **same** dataset rendered differently (Grid / Dashboard / Chart) → **View Switcher**,
  which is **not in this kit**. Flag the gap; do not substitute Tabs. If only the
  *presentation* of one dataset changes, it is not Tabs.
- Sequential steps → a Wizard, not Tabs.
- More than ~7 panels → reconsider the information architecture. When the row is narrower than its
  tabs (a side panel, a phone), the headless Tabs puts the tabs that don't fit into "N more" (see
  *Overflow*); that is for a narrow host, not for a long list of panels.

props.name: defaultValue
props.notes: Uncontrolled mode. **Required unless `value` is passed.**

props.name: value
props.notes: Controlled mode. `value` and `defaultValue` are exclusive.

props.name: onValueChange
props.notes: Controlled mode. `value` and `defaultValue` are exclusive.

props.name: size
props.notes: **These two only.** Default `regular`.

props.name: aria-label
props.notes: **Required.**

props.name: value
props.notes: Must match a Panel.

props.name: count
props.notes: Optional numeric badge.

props.name: disabled
props.notes: Skipped by arrow-key navigation.

props.name: unseen
props.notes: **Headless only.** The tab holds changes the person hasn't seen: set it when they arrive, clear it when the tab is opened. A hidden tab with `unseen` adds "· 1 new" to the "N more" control. The core trigger does not accept it.

props.name: value
props.notes: Must match a Trigger.

components.name: Text Area
components.purpose: Multi-line text entry with a label, optional hint, an error state and an optional live character count. Input's sibling: the same field anatomy, the same tokens, more lines.

status.label: Experimental
status.note: specced, built and tested; its Figma set is published in the library (built from scripts/figma/components/text-area.figma.js). Approved once the API has been reviewed; see GOVERNANCE.md.

components.whenToUse:
- Free text that runs past one line — a justification, an incident note, a rule description,
  a comment on an approval → **Text Area**.
- Single-line text or numeric-as-text → **Input**.
- Code, a query or a policy document that needs syntax highlighting → a code editor, **not in
  this kit**. Flag the gap; a Text Area is not an editor.
- Choosing from a set → Radio or Dropdown, **not in this kit**.

props.name: label
props.notes: **Required.**

props.name: value
props.notes: Controlled. Exclusive with `defaultValue`.

props.name: defaultValue
props.notes: Uncontrolled initial text. Exclusive with `value`.

props.name: onChange
props.notes: The native change event, as on Input. With `maxLength`, `event.target.value` is already within the limit.

props.name: hint
props.notes: Helper text. Wired via `aria-describedby`.

props.name: error
props.notes: Presence sets the error state; the string is the message.

props.name: size
props.notes: **These three only** — Input's set.

props.name: rows
props.notes: The minimum height, in lines. The field starts at this height and is never dragged shorter.

props.name: maxLength
props.notes: The limit, in characters. Shows a live `n / max` count below the field.

props.name: resize
props.notes: **These two only.** There is no horizontal and no both.

props.name: readOnly
props.notes: Focusable and selectable, not editable.

props.name: required
props.notes: Renders a `*` and sets the native attribute.

components.name: Toast
components.purpose: A short, floating **confirmation that something already happened** — "Policy saved", "Export started" — raised by the app, announced politely, and gone on its own or when dismissed. It is never the only record of what it says, never the only place an Undo lives, and never carries a decision.

status.label: Experimental
status.note: born in @omkarux/vela/headless (Base UI 1.9); there is no core implementation, and its Figma set is published in the library (built from scripts/figma/components/toast.figma.js). Approved once the API has settled; see GOVERNANCE.md.

components.whenToUse:
- An action the user just took **has completed**, and the page already shows the result — the row
  updated, the policy listed, the export queued in Reports — and a moment's confirmation helps →
  **Toast**.
- An event or condition the user **must read**, next to the thing it is about, that stays until
  it is resolved — a failed scan, a degraded connector, an error in a form → **Contextual Alert**
  (`contextual-alert.md`), in the page. A toast floats away from its subject and leaves on a timer.
- **Anything that failed** and needs the user to act — a save that did not save, a policy that did
  not apply → the error goes **where the work is**: an Input `error`, a Contextual Alert `major`.
  A toast never reports a failure (see *Hard constraints*, `toast-severity-closed`).
- A **question** — confirm, cancel, choose → **Dialog** (`dialog.md`); a destructive one →
  `variant="alert"`. A toast never asks: it has at most one action, and that action is a shortcut.
- An object's **ongoing** health → **Status Indicator**. A toast describes a moment, not a state.
- **Agentic actions.** When an agent acts on the user's behalf, the record of what it did — and the
  Undo — live in the place the agent's work is reviewed (an activity log, the object's history),
  and a toast may point at it. The toast is the notice, never the ledger.

props.name: placement
props.notes: **These three only.** Where the region sits. `end` follows the writing direction.

props.name: limit
props.notes: **These three only.** How many toasts show at once; older ones wait, hidden, and return as newer ones leave.

props.name: label
props.notes: The region's accessible name — the landmark F6 lands on.

props.name: dismissLabel
props.notes: The accessible name of every toast's close button.

props.name: children
props.notes: **Required.** The app.

props.name: add
props.notes: Raises a toast with the options below and returns its id. **Inside a `ToastProvider` only**; outside one `useToast()` throws a named error.

props.name: dismiss
props.notes: Dismisses the toast `add` returned that id for.

props.name: title
props.notes: **Required.** What happened, past tense: "Policy saved". The toast's accessible name.

props.name: description
props.notes: One sentence of detail, wired as the toast's description.

props.name: severity
props.notes: **These three only** — a subset of the Severity taxonomy.

props.name: action
props.notes: **At most one.** A shortcut — "View", "Undo" — to something that also exists on the page. Activating it runs `onClick` and dismisses the toast.

components.name: Toggle
components.purpose: A binary setting that takes effect **immediately**. No Save step.
components.whenToUse:
- Notifications on/off, dark mode, "enable this rule" → **Toggle**.
- Records intent until a Save click (accept terms, pick scope in a form) → **Checkbox**
  (`checkbox.md`, from `@omkarux/vela/headless`). Never substitute a Toggle.
- More than two states → not a Toggle.

props.name: label
props.notes: **Required.** A switch with no name is unusable by screen reader.

props.name: checked
props.notes: Controlled. Omit for uncontrolled. Exclusive with `defaultChecked`.

props.name: defaultChecked
props.notes: Uncontrolled initial state. Exclusive with `checked`.

props.name: onChange
props.notes: Receives the **next** value.

props.name: size
props.notes: **These two only.**

components.name: Tooltip
components.purpose: A short **supplementary label** for a control — what an abbreviated or iconic action does, the full text of a truncated value — shown on hover after a short rest and at once on keyboard focus, dismissed by Escape. **Text only.** A user who never sees it misses nothing they need.

status.label: Experimental
status.note: born in @omkarux/vela/headless (Base UI 1.9) with Popover and Dialog; there is no core implementation, and its Figma set is published in the library (built from scripts/figma/components/tooltip.figma.js). Approved once the API has settled; see GOVERNANCE.md.

components.whenToUse:
- A **phrase that explains a control** the user can already operate — "Download the last 24 hours
  as CSV" on an Export button → **Tooltip**.
- Anything the user can **act in** — a link, a button, a checkbox, a form → **Popover**
  (`popover.md`). A tooltip closes the moment the pointer leaves; nothing in it can be reached.
- An **infotip** behind an ⓘ icon, whose only job is to show the text → a **Popover**: the
  trigger's purpose is opening the panel, and a touch user can open a Popover but never sees a
  tooltip.
- Information the task **depends on** — a requirement, an error, why a control is disabled →
  **inline text** beside the control (Input's `hint`, Checkbox's `description`). Tooltips are
  hidden from touch users and are not reliably announced.
- An **icon-only** control's name → its `aria-label`. A tooltip may show the same words to sighted
  users, but it is never what names the control (see Hard constraints). A glyph-only control is an
  [**Icon Button**](icon-button.md), which brings its own label tooltip; don't wrap one in another.
- The **same words as the control's name**, for sighted users → **Tooltip** `kind="label"`: shown,
  and heard once. Any other words → the default `kind="description"`.

props.name: content
props.notes: **Required.** The text. A string: a tooltip never holds a link, a button, a list or bold.

props.name: children
props.notes: **Required.** The **one** element it describes — a `Button`, a native `<button>`, a link. It keeps its own accessible name.

props.name: placement
props.notes: **These four only**, as Popover. It flips when there is no room.

props.name: align
props.notes: **These three only.**

props.name: kind
props.notes: **These two only.** `description`: extra words, wired by `aria-describedby`. `label`: the trigger's own name, shown and not wired; `content` must equal that name.
